claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys have high saturation magnetization.
The starting alloy has a coercive field around, or no greater than approximately, 100 Oe.
Rapid thermal annealing of single-phase fcc FeCoNi promotes nanoscale chemical ordering.
Rapid thermal annealing may initiate cellular precipitation or produce L1_0-like ordered regions within an overall fcc matrix.
The proposed rapid thermal annealing permits limited atomic diffusion.
Localized chemical ordering increases magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Annealing-induced microstructural heterogeneities act as domain-wall pinning centers.
Increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy and domain-wall pinning increase the coercive field.
Rapid thermal annealing will increase coercivity significantly beyond the untreated value of approximately 100 Oe.
The coercivity increase can occur while high saturation magnetization remains largely unaffected.
The intervention can retain the single-phase fcc structure after annealing.

contradictions.description: The mediator permits an incipient cellular precipitation process and L1_0-like ordered regions, whereas the boundary requires retention of a single-phase fcc structure. A precipitated or crystallographically ordered L1_0-like constituent may violate that single-phase requirement unless it is explicitly defined as short-range ordering without a distinct phase.
